transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It is actually normal for many Beko washer-dryers to use a trickle of cold water during a drying cycle. This water cools the condenser inside the machine so that moisture from your clothes turns back into liquid and can be pumped away; if it didn't do this, the clothes would never dry. However, we should rule out a blockage which could cause excessive water usage or poor drying. Please check two things: first, ensure you haven't overloaded the drum (a dryer load is typically half the size of a wash load). Second, please switch off and unplug the machine, place towels under the bottom-front filter flap, unscrew the filter carefully to let any water drain out, and check if it is clogged with fluff or debris. Let me know what you find.

Thank you. I haven't opened the filter yet. The machine is only 2 months old, and I did look in the manual, which says water is used during drying for condensation. There is no error code, no leak, and the clothes come out dry. Is there really anything else I need to check?

No, there is nothing else you need to check. Since the manual suggests water is used for condensation and your clothes are coming out dry with no leaks or error codes, the machine is working exactly as designed. The water you hear running in and draining away is simply cooling the internal condenser so it can turn moisture from the clothes into liquid that gets pumped out. As long as the drying performance remains good, this is normal operation.
